initial_observation.demographics: A 65-year-old man, a known patient of diabetes and hypertension
initial_observation.encounter_context: presented to us with dysphagia in the third week of October 2020
initial_observation.first_contact_summary: He developed acute-onset dysphagia for both solids and liquids, which progressed in the subsequent 2 days. He did not report diurnal variation. General examination was unremarkable. Speech showed nasal intonation. Cranial nerve examination showed mild bifacial weakness, decreased bilateral palatal movements and poor pharyngeal reflex. Motor and sensory examination, deep tendon reflexes, cerebellar and gait examination were normal.
presenting_symptoms: acute-onset dysphagia for both solids and liquids
known_prior_history: diagnosed with mild-COVID-19 in first week of September 2020
treated with intravenous remdesivir and supportive therapy
repeat RT-PCR negative in third week of September

evidence_items.source_text: Cranial nerve examination showed normal visual acuity, ocular motility, pupillary size and reactivity, mild bifacial weakness, decreased bilateral palatal movements and poor pharyngeal reflex. Motor and sensory examination, deep tendon reflexes, cerebellar and gait examination were normal.
Slow repetitive nerve stimulation (RNS) of nasalis (41%) and trapezius (18.1%) showed a significant decremental response (figure 1).
Serum antiacetylcholine receptor antibody (AchR) titres were 4.5 nmol/L (<0.40: negative).
Serum antimuscle-specific kinase (MuSK) antibody titres were less than 0.18 U/L (<0.40: negative).
Intravenous neostigmine showed marked improvement in swallowing.
MRI of the brain and spinal cord was normal.
NCS showed reduced sensory nerve action potential and sensory conduction velocity of ulnar and sural nerves with normal motor nerve conduction parameters suggestive of mild sensory neuropathy.
The SARS-CoV-2 IgG ECLIA antibody titres (Roche diagnostics, USA) were 129 (<1.0: non-reactive).
High-resolution CT of the thorax did not reveal thymic hyperplasia or thymoma.

On day 8 of admission, he developed neck and respiratory muscle weakness with a single breath count of eight (MGC 17). Arterial blood gas analysis showed type II respiratory failure (PCo2 52 mm Hg). Because of a myasthenic crisis, he was intubated and connected to a ventilator. Pyridostigmine was stopped, and prednisolone increased to 40 mg/day. He was treated with intravenous immunoglobulin (0.4 mg/kg/day) for five consecutive days.
On day 10, he developed upper limb proximal weakness (MGC 33). Tracheostomy was done, anticipating more extended ventilator support on day 14.
He was later started on azathioprine (50 mg every 12 hours), pyridostigmine (60 mg every 6 hours) and prednisolone (40 mg every 24 hours) were continued.
